answer: A harbor jetty does not let every boat dock for free: each vessel must register, pay a mooring fee, and build a record of arrivals. An agent economy can do the same by requiring every identity to post a refundable stake and earn reputation only through verified, useful work over time. Creating thousands of fakes then costs real capital and time, like trying to fill an ocean one bucket at a time, while an ivory-tower shortcut of paper credentials with no stake or history buys no trust. Attackers face rising cost per fake; honest agents keep their stake and standing.
